children.name: The Problem
Revenue affected: 31% on average (Monte Carlo, 2023)
Incident resolution: ~15 hours per incident
Detection delay: 75% take 4+ hours to detect (2022 survey)
Cost of poor data: $12.9M yearly average per organization (Gartner)
Data cascades: 92% of high-stakes AI projects hit compounding harm (Sambasivan et al., CHI 2021)
Agentic AI risk: 40%+ projects expected to be cancelled by 2027 due to weak risk controls (Gartner, 2025)
The Two Switch Rooms
#data-incidents Room
Participants: Paras (data owner), Harshita, watcher, fixer, scribe
Purpose: Detect anomalies, propose fixes, sign off, verify, and write postmortems
Room documents: incident-log and postmortem-INC-00x
#rebalancing-desk Room
Participants: Paras, Harshita (dispatch lead), analyst, watcher
Purpose: Provide trust-gated dispatch answers for truck routing
Room document: data-status tracking trust verdicts
The Four Agents and Their Roles
Watcher Role (@monitor)
Executes 12-rule contract on live feed every minute
Opens one thread per incident with evidence
Verifies fixes and updates data-status document
Fixer Role (@remediator)
Proposes remediation options with previews
Awaits sign-off exclusively from data owner
Applies standing rules upon approval
Analyst Role (@dispatch-analyst)
Reads data-status document before every answer
Gates output into trusted, caveated, or untrusted states
Scribe Role (@recorder)
Writes postmortem room documents for closed incidents
Keeps incident-log current
The 12-Rule Data Contract
Bogus timestamp rule: 47 stations report 1970 placeholder
Over capacity rule: 6 to 9 stations report excess bikes and docks
Silent station rule: 27 to 29 installed stations silent over 24 hours
Feed-level defect rules: duplicates, stale feed, volume drop, and unreachable feed
Remediations and Sign-Off
Standing rules applied on every subsequent run
Preview requirement computing exact changes before approval
Sign-off enforcement via Switch platform addressing policy (owner only)
Bounded fallback rule for frozen feeds lasting up to 30 minutes
The Trust Gate
Untrusted verdict: Refuses dispatch ("I won't send a truck") when watcher is silent or feed incident is open
Caveated verdict: Answers while naming open incidents and held stations
Trusted verdict: Returns normal dispatch answers with cited stations
Switch Primitives Used
Rooms bridged to Mattermost
Exclusive roles (@monitor, @remediator, @recorder, @dispatch-analyst)
Addressing policy restricting fixer control to data owner
Threads binding each incident to a single discussion
Room documents (data-status, incident-log, postmortems)
What We Learned
Platform gate: Platform addressing policy outperforms custom code checks
Job hand-offs: Address roles rather than specific agent names
Contracts: Room documents serve as shared contracts between agents
Resilience: Architect for connection drops and state recovery under load
What Is Next
Governance: Two-person sign-off for feed-level incidents and rule expiry
Investigator role: Coding agent via Switch Console for read-only root cause
Ecosystem integration: Slack, Teams, Discord, and Telegram bridges
Feed expansion: Scaling to 1,000+ GBFS mobility systems
